findings.evidence: loadDetails queries every record in tree order. data.js:178-184 evicts the oldest completed cell at 128 cells without protecting validated entries. With 200 records, a completed sweep retains only the tail. The next refresh first reloads the evicted context/tree, then its early detail misses evict the retained tail before traversal reaches it. An unchanged refresh therefore transfers every detail body again, not just misses or changed bodies.
findings.requiredChange: Protect validated entries that the current sweep has not consumed. Keep context/tree entries from being displaced by detail scans. Preserve bounded eviction without letting sequential cache misses evict every upcoming hit.
findings.title: Full detail sweeps evict unchanged results before reuse
findings.validation: Use more than 128 records. Complete two unchanged refreshes and count helper body requests. Confirm retained unchanged details transfer no bodies and context/tree remain reusable.

findings.evidence: validate awaits a complete canonical load and observation pass for every token, serially. Each detail load rebuilds the tracker snapshot (data.ts:172), and observeRead rebuilds it again (observations.ts:31). core.js:19-20 routes only tracker operations through the long-running worker; validate gets a 60-second direct call. main.js:183 awaits the whole batch before refreshing the tree. A batch whose aggregate work exceeds that deadline cannot refresh, even when each individual read fits its deadline.
findings.requiredChange: Run batch validation through a cancellable, bounded worker with an appropriate aggregate deadline. Share canonical snapshot work within the batch instead of rebuilding the full tracker twice per detail.
findings.title: Serial validation runs behind the short direct-request deadline
findings.validation: Exercise a batch whose aggregate duration exceeds 60 seconds while individual reads remain valid. Confirm classifications complete, the tree refreshes, and target release stops pending validation work.

result.summary: Two engineering findings: cache-scan eviction defeats unchanged refreshes above 128 records; serial validation can exceed its transport deadline. Static review only. No source edits, builds, lint, tests, formatters, tracker changes, or worktree receipts.
